newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 3 to 822.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 3 to 822.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 822 as of September 27, down three from the prior week and 67 above the year-ago total of 755, Baker Hughes Inc. reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by five to 689, while rigs working offshore rose by two to 113. The number of rigs active in inland waters remained at 20.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Oklahoma, which showed a decrease of seven and Texas, which rose by five. Wyoming rose by five.

A total of 302 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down seven from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by four to 515, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained unchanged at five.
There were 179 rigs drilling directionally, 60 drilling horizontally and 583 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs fell by 20 to 239 versus 238 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Offshore Data Services said there were 164 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of September 27, unchanged from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 180, was 91.1 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean rose by one this week to 103 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 103, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count rose by one to 560 out of a total fleet of 606, making the utilization rate 92.4 percent.
